description: Cross-file call-graph corpus: a request-reading caller in one file reaches a shell/eval sink in another through an ordinary call edge. Each case directory is scanned as its own project root. Positives name the caller file and the line(s) where a CF-SINK-001 must be anchored; negatives must produce no CF-* finding at all. Seeded from the defects fixed on 2026-09-19 (BACKLOG XF-01, XF-02, XF-04, XF-05, XF-06); before that day none of the benchmark corpora exercised CrossFilePass, so a 17-finding change on a real repo moved no gated number (RT-19).

scoring.hit: every line in `lines` carries a CF-SINK-001 anchored in `caller_file`
scoring.clean: no CF-SINK-001 or CF-RETURN-001 anywhere in the case
scoring.gates: recall on expected=detect must be 1.0 and false positives on expected=clean must be 0

cases.description: The sink call is split across lines and a kwarg-line regex hit used to replace the call head as sink_line, leaving sink_params empty.
`from c import run_it as go` keyed the callee by its local alias.
Keyword-only and positional-only parameters were never indexed in the parameter summary.
A benign Safe.run defined after Shell.run masked it under a (file, name) key.
Positive twin of neg_constant_argument: the relay receives the request value.
handler reads request.args but passes a string literal to relay(); source status must not cross that edge.
The call resolves to Safe.run, which has no sink; Shell.run in the same file must not be attributed.
`import runner from './shell.js'` was keyed as the literal "default". Skipped when tree-sitter is not installed.
`svc = Svc()` at module level; the handler calls `svc.go(q)`, which shells out.
The module-level receiver is a `Safe`, whose same-named `go` only logs; `Svc.go` with the shell sink must not be chosen.
`self.runner` is typed only by the annotated `__init__(self, runner: Runner)`; `Runner.run` shells out.
Same shape with `runner: SafeRunner`, whose `run` only logs; `Runner.run` with the shell sink must not be chosen.
`Job(q)` runs `Job.__init__`, which shells out with its argument.
`Job.__init__` only stores its argument; the shell sink is in a different method that runs a constant command. The constructor edge must bind to `__init__`, not to whatever sink the class has.
`Request(...)` is httpx's class; an unrelated in-repo `Request` whose `__init__` shells out must not receive the constructor edge.
relay() calls a source-returning function but returns a constant, and handler's sink uses its own parameter, not relay()'s return.
Positive twin: relay() returns read_input(), and handler passes that value to a shell.
relay() really returns tainted data, but handler's sink uses its own parameter, not the captured return.
The source read and the call sit inside a `match` arm, which the statement walker did not descend into.
`from c import *` then a bare `run_it(q)` call.
`from pkg import run_it`, where pkg/__init__.py re-exports it from .impl.
`import pkg.impl` then `pkg.impl.run_it(q)`.
The handler reads req.query but passes the literal "ls" to runFixed.
Positive twin: runFixed(q) with q from req.query.
Same flow as js_tainted_argument, plus an unrelated file with a 3000-term string concatenation that must not abort the pass.
`open(q)` is the builtin; the same-file method `Store.open`, which shells out, must not receive the edge.
The callee runs a list-form subprocess call to a fixed program with no shell=True. The presence rule ns-aiml-076 matched it and marked it a command-injection sink.
List-form argv whose program is a shell run with -c is still a shell sink; the XF-26 list-form exemption must not cover it.
